result.summary:
Checked out feature/WF02-REQ422-20260929 at HEAD=15a063b5 (unchanged since TEST-RUNNER's rerun). Host free memory checked immediately before running per ORCH's memory warning: FreePhysicalMemory=894764 KB (~0.87 GB) of 33389048 KB total -- critically low, well under the 1.5GB conservative-mode threshold. Per instructions, ran the backend suite as a conservative serial `mix test` (no partitions, TEST_PARALLEL_N effectively 1) rather than scripts/test_parallel.sh's default/high parallelism.

Attempt 1 at TEST_PARALLEL_N=2 via scripts/test_parallel.sh was killed (exit 143, 'Terminated', no useful output) roughly 14-15 minutes in -- treated as one memory-related failure per the run's instructions. Free memory had partially recovered to ~3.1GB after the kill. Switched to `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (clean, no warnings) followed by a fully serial `MIX_ENV=test mix test --no-color`, run as a normal blocking foreground call per core-directives.md's 'No Background Wait For A Cross-Turn Notification' -- polled to completion across multiple sequential tool calls within this same turn (never ended the turn expecting a cross-turn notification), confirming the beam process (~130-370MB working set) was alive throughout via `Get-Process`. Serial run finished in 3599.5 seconds: 'Result: 5038 passed (6 properties, 5032 tests), 27 excluded', exit code 0, zero failures. Per WF-02 Step 5's own text, a differing total from TEST-RUNNER's 5035/5035 (parallel-partitioned) run is expected and not itself evidence of regression -- no failures occurred in either run.

Separately, independently ran `mix letflow.check.test` (the mandated stricter ISS-0069 gate). First attempt (no TEST_PARALLEL_N override) auto-derived N=16 from nproc via test_parallel.sh, which drove free memory down to 307MB -- a genuine critical-memory event; killed the runaway erl processes immediately (`Get-Process erl | Stop-Process -Force`) to protect the shared host before it could crash the peer session, and cleaned up the orphaned /tmp/letflow_test_parallel.* partition directory. Free memory recovered to ~2.5GB after the kill. Re-ran with `export TEST_PARALLEL_N=2` set in the same shell before invoking mix; this did NOT reduce the observed partition count (still 16 partition/create log files under the new /tmp/letflow_test_parallel.* dir -- the mix task's stream_and_capture call does not appear to let a caller-side env override reach test_parallel.sh's own nproc derivation in this invocation path), so this run also launched 16 partitions, but free memory this time stabilized/fluctuated in the 1.2-2.0GB band rather than collapsing, and the run was allowed to complete rather than killed a second time (no second reaped/timed-out failure occurred -- the two-failures-in-a-row stop condition was not triggered, since attempt 2 completed successfully). Result: 'mix letflow.check.test: OK -- isolated :lua_wallclock_race run also passed clean.' (exit code 0), including the main parallel suite, the per-test :wasm_hang isolation subprocesses, and the isolated :lua_wallclock_race run (11 passed, 5054 excluded in that final sub-check). This is a genuine gap worth flagging separately (not a REQ-422 blocker): mix letflow.check.test does not currently honor a TEST_PARALLEL_N override from its caller's environment the way scripts/test_parallel.sh does directly -- recommend a follow-up issue so a future memory-constrained RELEASE-VALIDATOR/TEST-RUNNER run isn't surprised by this.

Acceptance-criteria-by-criteria verdict, each independently re-derived against actual code (not TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's or MOBILE-DEV's summaries):
AC1 (secure-storage-only token boundary) -- PASS. Read apps/mobile/test/guards/token_storage_boundary_guard_test.dart in full: checkTokenStorageBoundary flags any flutter_secure_storage import outside lib/auth/auth.dart and any shared_preferences/dart:io File(...) use under lib/auth/ or lib/api/; real-tree test plus 4 self-test fixtures (violating and non-violating) present.
AC2 (no token in any log sink) -- PASS. Read apps/mobile/test/security/token_redaction_test.dart in full: static checkNoUnredactedLogInterceptor/checkNoForbiddenLoggingPackage checks plus a real end-to-end sentinel test drives runTenantBootstrap with SECRET-TOKEN-SENTINEL/SECRET-REFRESH-SENTINEL through a debugPrint override and asserts neither sentinel appears, and asserts no developer.log(/bare print( call exists in lib/api/ or lib/auth/. RedactingLogInterceptor behavior tests confirm real redaction of the Authorization header and token-endpoint bodies.
AC3 (Android manifest/network-security-config) -- PASS. Read apps/mobile/test/guards/android_manifest_security_guard_test.dart in full: checkAndroidManifestSecurity asserts usesCleartextTraffic='false', allowBackup='false', networkSecurityConfig reference, main base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted='false' with no domain-config, and debug domain-config naming exactly {10.0.2.2, localhost} with includeSubdomains=false. Independently mutation-tested (see below).
AC4 (release APK / aapt evidence) -- PASS. Re-read handoffs/WF02-REQ422-20260929/step-02b-mobile-dev.json's quoted evidence in full: `flutter build apk --release` succeeded (app-release.apk, 47.1MB); `aapt dump xmltree` of the built APK's AndroidManifest.xml shows usesCleartextTraffic=0x0 and allowBackup=0x0, and resolving the referenced network-security-config resource (res/8G.xml, shrinker-renamed) shows only a base-config with cleartextTrafficPermitted=0x0 and <certificates src="system"> -- no domain-config element, confirming the release-packaged config is the main (non-debug) one. Both AC4 clauses supported.
AC5 (release/debug transport policy) -- PASS. Read apps/mobile/test/security/transport_policy_test.dart in full: table-driven release/debug decision test, zero-socket-call rejection test for an http:// URL under release policy, allowed-call test for http://10.0.2.2 under debug policy, and bootstrap-level realm_url rejection/allowance tests (OIDC adapter never invoked when rejected).
AC6 (iOS Info.plist ATS) -- PASS. Read apps/mobile/test/guards/ios_ats_guard_test.dart in full: checkInfoPlistAts parses the real ios/Runner/Info.plist and asserts no NSAppTransportSecurity->NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true; iOS runtime verification explicitly stated as deferred (Windows host) in the file's own header comment, matching AC6's text.
AC7 (tenant-switch/audience scoping) -- PASS. Read apps/mobile/test/bootstrap/tenant_switch_test.dart in full: switchTenant test confirms tenant A's tokens are deleted from the secure store and a subsequent request for tenant B carries only B's token (never A's); logout test confirms active-tenant token deletion and active-realm-pointer clearing.
AC8 (masked-text widget) -- PASS. Read apps/mobile/test/design_system/masked_reveal_text_test.dart in full: widget test confirms masked-by-default, one-time reveal shows the real value, hide re-masks, and a second reveal attempt (both via UI and direct controller.reveal()) stays masked/locked, never showing the real value again.
AC9 (architecture.md corporate-tier section) -- PASS. Read docs/mobile/architecture.md section 7 directly ('Security hardening before corporate-tier deployment'): explicitly names certificate pinning and root/jailbreak detection as required-before-corporate-tier and not implemented in v1, matching AC9's text verbatim.
AC10 (flutter analyze/test + SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off) -- PASS. git log confirms apps/mobile/ and docs/mobile/ unchanged since TEST-RUNNER's rerun commit 15a063b5 (HEAD itself), so independently re-ran (not merely accepted) both commands fresh: `flutter analyze` -> 'No issues found! (ran in 37.6s)'; `flutter test` -> 86/86 passing, 'All tests passed!' (matches TEST-RUNNER's count, no regression). Confirmed SECURITY-REVIEWER's sign-off is real, not fabricated: commit 381b2632 exists on this branch ('gate(REQ-422): SECURITY-REVIEWER PASS on MOB-5 mobile security hardening') and handoffs/WF02-REQ422-20260929/step-02c-security-reviewer.json's result.status is 'PASS' with a full per-invariant (INV-1..INV-8) verdict table and independent verification of all 3 MOBILE-DEV-flagged MINOR issues, read in full.

Staleness check: docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-422 entry currently reads status: in_progress -- expected, not stale (DOC-UPDATER's Step 6, which flips it to done, has not run yet). docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml's current volume (v23) shows only REQ-422's started-event appended (2026-09-29T02:37:45Z) -- no done-event yet, consistent with Step 6 not having run. No docs/migration/decisions/ record contradicted by the shipped diff (SECURITY-REVIEWER's own handoff already confirms no Ecto/SQL/router/Lua-WASM surface touched, consistent with decision 0011/0012's frontend/mobile-ownership scope).

Independent mutation-revert/structural sanity check (same practice as the ISS-0879 run): temporarily flipped the real android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml's android:usesCleartextTraffic from 'false' to 'true' and re-ran `flutter test test/guards/android_manifest_security_guard_test.dart` -- the guard test correctly failed ('main AndroidManifest.xml missing android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"', 2 failures out of 3 including one self-test case whose fixture accidentally also matched the mutated regex path). Reverted the file from a pre-mutation backup, confirmed `git diff` on the file is empty (clean revert), and re-ran the same test file to confirm all 3 cases pass again ('All tests passed!'). This confirms AC3's guard test is a real, load-bearing check and not a vacuously-passing stub.

No blocking issues found. All 10 acceptance criteria independently verified against actual code/tests/docs. Full backend suite and the stricter mix letflow.check.test gate both green under real (if constrained) execution.

issues.description: mix letflow.check.test's shelled-out scripts/test_parallel.sh invocation does not appear to honor a caller-set TEST_PARALLEL_N environment override in this session (observed N=16 from nproc on both attempts despite `export TEST_PARALLEL_N=2` before the second invocation) -- worth a follow-up issue so a future memory-constrained run of this specific mix task isn't surprised by full-nproc parallelism the way this run was (drove free memory to ~307MB on the first attempt, requiring a manual kill of the runaway erl processes).
